\chapter{Mother and Elder Siblings}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মা} (mā)}{মা (mā)}]{\bn{মা} (mā) — a mother}

\label{lesson:BN-C481-ma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for smoking, then the Bengali for to shed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মা}}
\textbf{\bn{মা}} — \emph{mā} — \textquotedblleft{}a mother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{মা} \bn{রোজ} \bn{সকালে} \bn{চা} \bn{বানান।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmār mā roj sôkāle chā bānān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother makes tea every morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মা}} (\emph{mā}) comes from Sanskrit \emph{mātṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}mother\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10016), which CDIAL lists in this Bengali form; \bn{মেয়ে} (taught), a girl, is filed under the same entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmār mā roj sôkāle chā bānān.} — My mother makes tea every morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for smoking, then the Bengali for to shed, then say \emph{mā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দাদা} (dādā)}{দাদা (dādā)}]{\bn{দাদা} (dādā) — an elder brother}

\label{lesson:BN-C481-dada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to shed, then the Bengali for a mother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দাদা}}
\textbf{\bn{দাদা}} — \emph{dādā} — \textquotedblleft{}an elder brother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{দাদা} \bn{শহরে} \bn{চাকরি} \bn{করেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmār dādā shôhôre chākri kôren.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My elder brother has a job in the city.
\end{quote}

\bn{ভাই} (taught) is a brother in general, often the younger; \bn{দাদা} is the elder, and the word you call him by.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দাদা}} (\emph{dādā}) is listed by CDIAL for Bengali, as both a grandfather and an elder brother, under a reconstructed nursery word (CDIAL 6261).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmār dādā shôhôre chākri kôren.} — My elder brother has a job in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to shed, then the Bengali for a mother, then say \emph{dādā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দাদা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An elder brother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দিদি} (didi)}{দিদি (didi)}]{\bn{দিদি} (didi) — an elder sister}

\label{lesson:BN-C481-didi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a mother, then the Bengali for an elder brother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দিদি}}
\textbf{\bn{দিদি}} — \emph{didi} — \textquotedblleft{}an elder sister\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দিদি} \bn{আমাকে} \bn{সাঁতার} \bn{শেখাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{didi āmāke sā̃tār shekhālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My elder sister taught me to swim.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দিদি}} (\emph{didi}) is listed by CDIAL for Bengali, as an elder sister, under a reconstructed nursery word (CDIAL 6327).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{didi}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a mother, then the Bengali for an elder brother, then say \emph{didi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বউদি} (boudi)}{বউদি (boudi)}]{\bn{বউদি} (boudi) — an elder brother's wife; a sister-in-law}

\label{lesson:BN-C481-boudi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an elder brother, then the Bengali for an elder sister.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বউদি}}
\textbf{\bn{বউদি}} — \emph{boudi} — \textquotedblleft{}an elder brother's wife; a sister-in-law\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বউদি} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{পায়েস} \bn{রান্না} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{boudi āmāder jônyô pāyes rānnā kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister-in-law made rice pudding for us.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বউদি}} (\emph{boudi}) puts \emph{bou}, \textquotedblleft{}wife, bride\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{vadhū} (CDIAL 11250), with \bn{দিদি}, elder sister: the elder brother's wife, called by a sister's name.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{boudi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{boudi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{boudi āmāder jônyô pāyes rānnā kôrlen.} — My sister-in-law made rice pudding for us.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an elder brother, then the Bengali for an elder sister, then say \emph{boudi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঠাকুমা} (ṭhākumā)}{ঠাকুমা (ṭhākumā)}]{\bn{ঠাকুমা} (ṭhākumā) — a paternal grandmother}

\label{lesson:BN-C481-thakuma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an elder sister, then the Bengali for an elder brother's wife.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঠাকুমা}}
\textbf{\bn{ঠাকুমা}} — \emph{ṭhākumā} — \textquotedblleft{}a paternal grandmother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঠাকুমা} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{রাজার} \bn{গল্প} \bn{বলতেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭhākumā āmāder rājār gôlpo bôlten.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother used to tell us stories about kings.
\end{quote}

\bn{দিদিমা} (taught) is the mother's mother; \bn{ঠাকুমা} is the father's.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঠাকুমা}} (\emph{ṭhākumā}) puts \emph{ṭhākur}, a title of respect, from Sanskrit \emph{ṭhakkura}, \textquotedblleft{}a deity; a title\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5488), with \bn{মা}, mother.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhākumā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhākumā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhākumā āmāder rājār gôlpo bôlten.} — Grandmother used to tell us stories about kings.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an elder sister, then the Bengali for an elder brother's wife, then say \emph{ṭhākumā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ঠাকুমা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A paternal grandmother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
